title: Agent Documentation Template Library
summary: Reusable templates for scoped agent work, repository instructions, tool governance, evaluation, handoffs, approvals, and release learning.

sections.title: Task Intake And Contracts
sections.description: Templates that convert broad intent into bounded, reviewable work before an agent edits files.

sections.title: Repository Instructions
sections.description: Templates that teach agents how to work in a repository without expanding their autonomy silently.

sections.title: Planning And Handoffs
sections.description: Templates for plans, specialist ownership, multi-agent coordination, and transfer of responsibility.

sections.title: Review And Approval Gates
sections.description: Templates for pull requests, human review, sensitive actions, and release decisions.

sections.title: Tools, MCP, And Permissions
sections.description: Templates that document tool access, MCP risk, roots, secrets, and allowed execution boundaries.

sections.title: Evaluation And Observability
sections.description: Templates for trace review, regression tests, failure analysis, and reliability evidence.

sections.title: Memory, State, And Release Learning
sections.description: Templates for durable state, decisions, retrospectives, and cross-session learning.

templates.title: Accessibility Checklist
templates.goal: Define accessibility expectations and evidence for UI or documentation changes.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when agent work changes visible UI, navigation, forms, tables, or learning content.
expectations: Accessibility checks are tied to affected routes.
Keyboard and responsive behavior are checked.
Evidence is linked from the PR.

templates.title: Agent Evaluation Plan
templates.goal: Define task-level, trace-level, and release-level evaluation for agent workflows.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before changing prompts, tools, routing, handoffs, models, or guardrails.

templates.title: Agent Failure Analysis
templates.goal: Classify agent failures by prompt, context, tool, state, handoff, evaluation, or governance root cause.
templates.suggestedUse: Use after failed tasks, unsafe tool calls, incorrect PRs, broken releases, or drift reports.
expectations: Root cause is specific enough to fix.
A regression test or guardrail is added.
The action owner and due date are clear.

templates.title: Agent Validation Workflow
templates.goal: Run repeatable validation for agent-generated changes in CI.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when agent work needs automated checks, artifacts, and release evidence.

templates.title: Audit Trail
templates.goal: Record agent decisions, tool calls, approvals, and evidence in a durable trail.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when accountability, compliance, or multi-agent traceability matters.
expectations: Tool use and approvals are visible.

templates.title: CodeQL Workflow
templates.goal: Run semantic security analysis for code touched by agents.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when agent changes touch code paths where static analysis evidence is required.
expectations: Security scanning is automatic and repeatable.

templates.title: Error Analysis
templates.goal: Classify errors and convert failures into evals, tests, or template updates.
templates.suggestedUse: Use after wrong answers, bad PRs, failed checks, tool mistakes, or source drift.

templates.title: Security Scan Evidence
templates.goal: Record static, dependency, secret, or policy scan evidence for agent changes.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when agent work touches code, workflows, dependencies, secrets, or deploy paths.
expectations: Evidence is linked in the PR.

templates.title: Trace Review Record
templates.goal: Capture tool calls, handoffs, guardrail trips, and evidence from an agent run.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for debugging agent behavior and building eval cases from real failures.
expectations: Sensitive trace data is redacted before sharing.

templates.title: Tuning Log
templates.goal: Record prompt, model, tool, route, or guardrail changes and their evaluation impact.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when improving agent behavior after evals, failures, or source-drift findings.
expectations: Baseline and new results are compared.

templates.title: Agent Memory Policy
templates.goal: Define what agent memory may store, reuse, redact, or forget.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when lessons cover short-term, long-term, external, or shared memory.
expectations: Memory policy separates facts from assumptions.
Sensitive data is blocked or redacted.
Retention and review cadence are explicit.

templates.title: Agent Release Retrospective
templates.goal: Record what changed, what evidence passed, what failed, and what the next template or eval improvement should be.
templates.suggestedUse: Use after agent-assisted releases, workflow migrations, source updates, or template-library changes.
expectations: Misses become eval or template changes.

templates.title: Agent State Record
templates.goal: Capture durable workflow state for long-running agent tasks.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when lessons mention state, checkpoints, resumes, or external memory.

templates.title: Context Handoff
templates.goal: Transfer relevant context between sessions without carrying stale or private data.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when compacting, resuming, or handing off agent work.
expectations: Only relevant context is carried forward.

templates.title: Decision Log
templates.goal: Record durable decisions and why they were made.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when lessons mention governance, state, memory, review, or source-drift decisions.
expectations: The log separates evidence from preference.

templates.title: Memory And State Record
templates.goal: Keep durable state explicit across long-running or resumed agent work.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when an agent continues across sessions, summarizes work, compacts context, or stores durable memory.
expectations: State can be audited outside chat.
Assumptions are not mistaken for facts.

templates.title: Recovery Plan
templates.goal: Define how to recover when an agent workflow fails or produces unsafe output.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for production, release, multi-agent, or tool-enabled workflows.

templates.title: Resume Checkpoint
templates.goal: Create a checkpoint that lets an agent resume safely after interruption or context compaction.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for long tasks, paused sessions, or handoffs.
expectations: Stale context is checked before continuing.

templates.title: Stale Context Checklist
templates.goal: Check whether assumptions, sources, memory, or instructions have expired.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before resuming long-running work or relying on prior source-grounded content.

templates.title: Agent Handoff
templates.goal: Summarize current state and transfer work to another agent or human reviewer.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for resumed work, specialist transitions, or multi-agent workflows.
expectations: The receiver can continue without chat history.
Open risks and decisions are explicit.
Ownership of the next action is clear.

templates.title: Agent Plan
templates.goal: Require a plan before edits, including assumptions, files, validation, risks, and decision points.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before allowing an agent to make non-trivial or cross-file changes.
expectations: The plan can be approved or rejected before edits.
The plan maps each action to validation.
Risky work has named review gates.

templates.title: Agent Roles
templates.goal: Define responsibilities, boundaries, and handoff rules for each agent role.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when planner, builder, tester, reviewer, security, or release agents coordinate.
expectations: Each role has one clear responsibility.
Handoffs do not create ownership gaps.

templates.title: Conflict Log
templates.goal: Track conflicts between agents, tools, requirements, or source documents.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when multi-agent work or source-grounded content produces incompatible recommendations.

templates.title: Multi-Agent Handoff Contract
templates.goal: Define when ownership transfers between planner, builder, tester, reviewer, or specialist agents.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when more than one agent or specialist workflow participates in the same delivery chain.
expectations: Only one agent owns the next action.

templates.title: Multi-Agent Plan
templates.goal: Plan coordinated work across multiple specialist agents.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when planner, builder, tester, reviewer, or release agents share one goal.

templates.title: AGENTS.md
templates.goal: Define agent operating rules, local scope, approval points, and evidence requirements.
templates.suggestedUse: Use at the repository root, and add nested AGENTS.md files for areas with stricter local rules.
expectations: Nearest instructions are authoritative for a path.
Agents know when not to continue.

templates.title: Copilot Repository Instructions
templates.goal: Give Copilot and coding agents repository-specific build, test, validation, architecture, and safety instructions.
templates.suggestedUse: Use as the root repository instruction file and update it whenever commands, ownership, or sensitive areas change.
expectations: The instructions are short enough to be read every session.
Sensitive areas and approval gates are explicit.

templates.title: Copilot Setup Steps Workflow
templates.goal: Prepare repository dependencies and environment setup for Copilot coding agent sessions.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when Copilot needs deterministic setup before building, testing, or validating work.
expectations: Secrets are not exposed in logs.
The workflow mirrors local repository instructions.

templates.title: Agent Approval Gates
templates.goal: Document which actions require human approval before the agent continues.
templates.suggestedUse: Use in regulated, production, security, deployment, data, or MCP/tool-enabled workflows.
expectations: Approval rules are tied to risk.
Bypass conditions are exceptional and logged.

templates.title: Approval Policy
templates.goal: Define risk-based approval rules for agent actions.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for high-risk agent actions, production controls, security, data, or compliance work.
expectations: Bypass rules are exceptional and logged.

templates.title: Autonomy Matrix
templates.goal: Map agent autonomy levels to allowed actions and approval gates.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when deciding how much independence an agent should have for a task or domain.
expectations: Rollback is defined for each tier.

templates.title: CODEOWNERS Template
templates.goal: Define ownership rules so agent changes route to accountable reviewers.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when lessons mention CODEOWNERS, sensitive paths, or owner review for agent-generated changes.
expectations: Reviewers are teams or users with authority.
The PR explains why each owner is required.

templates.title: Escalation Paths
templates.goal: Define how agents escalate ambiguity, risk, tool failures, and approval needs.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when agent tasks can encounter blocked tools, unclear requirements, or sensitive decisions.

templates.title: Guardrails
templates.goal: Document behavioral, tool, data, and approval guardrails for agents.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for safety-sensitive tasks, compliance, responsible AI, or production workflows.

templates.title: Pull Request Template
templates.goal: Make every agent PR reviewable through scope, evidence, tests, risk, and rollback information.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for all PRs, with extra rigor for agent-generated changes.
expectations: A reviewer can decide from the PR body.
Validation output is linked or summarized.
Risk and rollback are not hidden.

templates.title: Responsible AI Risk Review
templates.goal: Assess fairness, reliability, privacy, safety, transparency, and accountability risks.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for agent workflows affecting people, sensitive data, decisions, or user-facing automation.

templates.title: Agent Task Contract
templates.goal: Define a reusable contract for issue-to-PR agent work.
templates.suggestedUse: Use when an issue needs more governance than a short issue form can express.
expectations: The contract names the owner of each risk.
The contract names the final evidence required.
The contract defines when the agent must stop.

templates.title: Agent Task Issue Template
templates.goal: Create a task record that names the business goal, scope, constraints, evidence, and stop conditions before an agent starts work.
templates.suggestedUse: Use for every agent-assigned issue, especially work that touches tests, workflows, security, user-facing behavior, or source-grounded content.
expectations: The issue is understandable without reading chat history.
The agent can identify what is allowed and what is blocked.
A reviewer can verify completion from PR evidence.

templates.title: Environment Constraints
templates.goal: Document runtime, network, filesystem, secret, and deployment constraints for agent work.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before running agents in local, CI, cloud, or sandboxed environments.
expectations: Secrets and write surfaces are protected.

templates.title: MCP Server Review
templates.goal: Review MCP server capability, roots, tools, secrets, transport, and autonomous-use risk before enabling it.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before adding or changing an MCP server for Copilot, code review, an IDE, or a custom agent.
expectations: Tools are mapped to business need.
Root boundaries and auth are explicit.
Autonomous use is accepted or rejected by an accountable owner.

templates.title: MCP Tool Policy
templates.goal: Define which MCP tools are allowed, restricted, or forbidden.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before enabling MCP servers or toolsets for agents.

templates.title: Tool Permission Matrix
templates.goal: Inventory allowed tools, denied tools, escalation rules, and data exposure boundaries.
templates.suggestedUse: Use before enabling shell, browser, MCP, deployment, database, or third-party integration tools.
expectations: Secrets and write actions have gates.
Each tool has an observable audit signal.
